notes: The sheet is an English list of wording and spelling remarks. The top reference and part of its first line are washed out; only fragments are recoverable. There is no title and no stated page count.

The upper list runs through p.100 and is crossed by two long oblique strokes. A horizontal rule separates the continuing entries for pp.102–115 below. The exact drawn marks, local cancellations and the later supralinear in are retained.

At p.89 the writer offers or alternatively to have made me, asks whether very is necessary, and gives an alternative would be last, not least,. At p.90 line -8 the proposed replacement would give better flow of words.
The right note at p.90 states 4 occurences on this page. The same region has a cancelled double-negative remark and an entry ending (twice).
At p.91 the two phrases in view of and with the view to are distinguished by previous happenings versus future hopes & expectations; the parenthetical examples contain two local cancellations.

The p.92 suggestion remains qualified by probably and records repetition at line -3. The p.99 notation remark reads X, cancelled ha, Y have got changed to F, G it seems.; its final qualification is retained.
Sent 19/12/83 appears at the right above the horizontal rule. It is a dispatch note, not a heading or an inferred composition date.

The lower block revisits commute with, contractions and spellings, including developing (single p.), the Kan / Khan|Khân comparison, and the short repeated underline under the medial s of relationships. The numbered page/line references are references to a text being corrected, not this sheet’s pagination.
The lower-left 20 is an archive sheet number and is represented only as a TeX comment. No mathematical claim appears that warranted a substantive mathematical check.

The two oblique strokes are reproduced as visible crossings without deciding whether every word in the upper block was cancelled. The side rules, faint far-left trace and isolated wavy stroke are likewise drawn without an assigned editorial meaning. The faint trace’s origin and exact endpoints are uncertain; its visible geometry is approximated.

Root retained uncertainty for the erased top dash, p.87 punctuation group, p.102 opener, buried old letters and final colon. The p.88 point remains a period because a bounded pale disc occupies the normal baseline position. No punctuation or missing parenthesis was supplied merely to regularize the prose.
coverage: All three full readings and all proposed differences were compared. Root inspected fourteen retained reader crops and made four new narrow drawing crops because no reader had cropped those whole marks. The final inventory has 57 rows, including all local deletion/insertion/underline elements and the line drawings; full-page rules are listed first, followed by text order and nested elements. No clipped words were restored from recurring text. H is descriptive only. The table-context input omission was corrected equally for all readers during their crop stage. Reader A attempted a compilation contrary to the source prompt; it failed at the missing-format stage. That attempt and its diagnostic remain documented; root performed static checks only and no compilation completed.
